analysis_mode_options.fast: Regex-only scanning — fastest, lowest cost, deterministic
analysis_mode_options.deep: LLM-only analysis — slower, full reasoning, best coverage
analysis_mode_options.hybrid: Regex first, then LLM for ambiguous/complex cases (recommended)

doc_scanning._comment: Documentation/text files are scanned for hardcoded secrets only. Code-flow vuln patterns (SSRF, path traversal, injection) are noise in non-executable docs, but a real credential in a README is still a real leak. Set secrets_only=false to scan docs like code.

test_scanning._comment: Test files are skipped entirely. Test fixtures are dominated by fake sentinels, dummy credentials, and negative-test URLs that produce almost only false positives. Patterns ending in / match a path segment; others are basename globs. Set skip_tests=false to scan tests like production code.

llm_app_scanning._comment: Opt-in. Set enabled=true if this project's application code CALLS an LLM (OpenAI/Anthropic/LangChain/Ollama/Bedrock/etc.). Adds OWASP-LLM-Top-10 checks for developer-accident classes: prompt injection (untrusted input into prompts), unsafe handling of LLM output (output into eval/shell/SQL/innerHTML), excessive agency (agents with shell/code tools), secrets-in-prompt, system-prompt exposure, and missing token/timeout limits. Off by default because these checks only make sense for LLM-backed apps and would be noise elsewhere.

auth_scanning._comment: 'auto' (default) detects whether this project uses authentication by checking package.json/requirements.txt/Pipfile/pyproject.toml/setup.cfg against the library lists below, and gates the access-control checks (missing_auth_middleware, idor_heuristic, admin_role_check) on that result — silent for public APIs/internal tools that don't use auth, active for anything that pulls in an auth library. Set to true/false to override detection manually. The password/JWT/session hygiene checks below (weak_password_hashing, jwt_missing_expiration, session_cookie_flags) are self-scoped — they only fire on unambiguous password-hashing/JWT-signing/session-config syntax — and always run regardless of this setting.

security_relevant._comment: In hybrid mode, files whose name/path contains any of these substrings ALWAYS get contextual analysis, regardless of the request->sink token heuristic. Fixes inverted coverage: secret-handling modules (config, logging) rarely look like request handlers, so the token heuristic misses exactly the files that matter most.

post_install_audit_options.pip_audit: Runs pip-audit after pip install (requires: pip install pip-audit)
post_install_audit_options.npm_audit: Runs npm audit after npm install (built into npm)
